base64.faqTitle: คำถามที่พบบ่อย

faqs.q: What is Base64 encoding?
faqs.a: Base64 is a binary-to-text encoding scheme that converts binary data into ASCII characters. It's commonly used to transmit data safely over text-based protocols like HTTP and email.

faqs.q: Is Base64 encoding the same as encryption?
faqs.a: No. Base64 is an encoding scheme, not encryption. Anyone can decode Base64 data. It's meant for data transport, not security.

faqs.q: Does this tool support UTF-8?

faqs.q: What is URL encoding?
faqs.a: URL encoding replaces unsafe ASCII characters with a '%' followed by two hex digits. This ensures special characters are safely transmitted in URLs.

faqs.q: What's the difference between encodeURI and encodeURIComponent?
faqs.a: encodeURI encodes a full URL but preserves characters like :, /, ?, &. encodeURIComponent encodes everything including those characters, making it suitable for query parameter values.

faqs.q: When should I URL encode?
faqs.a: Always URL encode when passing user input as query parameters, form data, or any URL component that may contain special characters like spaces, &, =, or #.

faqs.q: What is a hash function?
faqs.a: A hash function takes input data and produces a fixed-size string of characters (hash). The same input always produces the same hash, but you cannot reverse a hash back to the original data.

faqs.q: Which hash algorithm should I use?
faqs.a: SHA-256 is recommended for most purposes. SHA-512 offers more security. MD5 and SHA-1 are considered weak for security but are still used for checksums.

faqs.q: Is my data safe?
faqs.a: Yes. All hash computation happens in your browser using the Web Crypto API. No data is sent to any server.

faqs.q: What is a UUID?
faqs.a: UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) is a 128-bit number used to uniquely identify information. Version 4 UUIDs are randomly generated, making collision probability astronomically low.

faqs.q: Are UUIDs truly unique?
faqs.a: While not mathematically guaranteed, UUID v4 has 2^122 possible values. The probability of generating a duplicate is essentially zero for practical purposes.

faqs.q: When should I use UUIDs?
faqs.a: Use UUIDs as database primary keys, API resource identifiers, session tokens, or any time you need a unique identifier without a central authority.

faqs.q: What is a Unix timestamp?
faqs.a: A Unix timestamp is the number of seconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC (the Unix epoch). It's a universal way to represent time in computing.

faqs.q: What's the difference between seconds and milliseconds?
faqs.a: Unix timestamps in seconds are 10 digits (e.g., 1700000000), while milliseconds are 13 digits (e.g., 1700000000000). JavaScript uses milliseconds, most systems use seconds.

faqs.q: Does this tool handle timezones?
faqs.a: Yes. The tool shows both UTC and your local timezone when converting timestamps, so you can see the exact time in both.

faqs.a: JWT (JSON Web Token) is a compact, URL-safe token format used for authentication and information exchange. It contains a header, payload, and signature.

faqs.q: Is it safe to decode JWTs here?

faqs.q: Can this tool verify JWT signatures?

faqs.a: CSS minification removes whitespace, comments, and unnecessary characters from CSS code to reduce file size and improve page load speed.

faqs.q: What are number bases?
faqs.a: Number bases (or radixes) are systems for representing numbers. Common bases: binary (base 2), octal (base 8), decimal (base 10), and hexadecimal (base 16).

faqs.q: Why do programmers use hexadecimal?
faqs.a: Hexadecimal is compact and maps neatly to binary — each hex digit represents exactly 4 binary bits. It's widely used for colors, memory addresses, and byte values.

faqs.q: What's binary used for?
faqs.a: Binary (base 2) is the fundamental language of computers. Understanding binary helps with bitwise operations, networking (IP addresses), and low-level programming.

faqs.q: What is chmod?
faqs.a: chmod (change mode) is a Unix/Linux command that sets file and directory permissions. It controls who can read, write, and execute files.

faqs.q: What does 755 mean?
faqs.a: 755 means: owner can read/write/execute (7), group can read/execute (5), others can read/execute (5). It's the standard permission for directories and scripts.

faqs.q: What's the difference between numeric and symbolic notation?
faqs.a: Numeric uses octal digits (755). Symbolic uses letters (rwxr-xr-x). They represent the same permissions — numeric is more compact, symbolic is more readable.

xml-formatter.seoContent: XML (Extensible Markup Language) is widely used for data exchange, configuration files, and web services like SOAP APIs. Properly formatted XML improves readability and helps identify structural errors quickly. This tool formats, minifies, and validates XML documents in your browser. It supports large XML files, preserves CDATA sections and comments, and highlights syntax for easier inspection. Whether you are debugging API responses or cleaning up configuration files, this formatter handles it all without sending your data to any server.

faqs.q: How do I format XML online?
faqs.a: Paste your XML into the input area and click Format. The tool will indent and structure your XML with proper nesting and line breaks.

faqs.q: Can I minify XML to reduce file size?

faqs.q: Does this tool validate XML syntax?
faqs.a: Yes. The formatter checks for well-formedness including matching tags, proper nesting, and valid attribute syntax. Errors are highlighted with line numbers.

csv-json.seoContent: CSV and JSON are two of the most common data formats in software development. CSV excels for spreadsheet data and database exports, while JSON is the standard for APIs and web applications. This tool converts between the two formats instantly in your browser. It automatically detects headers from CSV files, handles quoted fields with commas, and produces clean JSON output. When converting JSON to CSV, it flattens nested objects and arrays into tabular columns. Perfect for transforming data between different systems without writing scripts.

faqs.q: How do I convert CSV to JSON online?
faqs.a: Paste your CSV data into the input area. The first row is used as headers. Click Convert to generate a JSON array of objects.

faqs.q: Can I convert JSON back to CSV?
faqs.a: Yes. Switch to JSON → CSV mode, paste your JSON array, and the tool will generate a CSV file with headers derived from object keys.

faqs.q: Does it handle nested JSON objects?
faqs.a: Yes. Nested objects are flattened using dot notation (e.g., address.city) when converting to CSV columns.

howToUseSteps: Select the conversion direction: CSV → JSON or JSON → CSV

http-status.seoContent: HTTP status codes are three-digit numbers returned by servers to indicate the result of a client request. They are grouped into five classes: 1xx (informational), 2xx (success), 3xx (redirection), 4xx (client errors), and 5xx (server errors). Understanding these codes is essential for API development, debugging network issues, and building robust web applications. This reference tool lets you quickly look up any status code, understand its meaning, and learn when to use it in your own APIs. It covers all standard codes defined in RFC 7231 and common extensions.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 401 and 403?
faqs.a: 401 Unauthorized means the client has not provided valid authentication credentials. 403 Forbidden means the client is authenticated but does not have permission to access the resource.

faqs.q: When should I use 200 vs 201 vs 204?
faqs.a: Use 200 OK for successful GET requests, 201 Created when a new resource is created (POST), and 204 No Content for successful requests with no response body (DELETE).

faqs.q: What does a 502 Bad Gateway error mean?
faqs.a: 502 means the server acting as a gateway received an invalid response from an upstream server. It usually indicates a problem with the backend service, not the client.

howToUseSteps: Browse the status codes by category (1xx through 5xx)
Click on any code to see its detailed description
Use the search box to find a specific code quickly
Review the use cases to understand when to return each code
useCases: Designing REST API response codes
Debugging HTTP errors in web applications
Learning about HTTP protocol standards
Documenting API error handling behavior

mime-types.seoContent: MIME types (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions) define the nature and format of a document or file. Web servers use MIME types in Content-Type headers to tell browsers how to handle files. Getting the MIME type wrong can cause browsers to download files instead of displaying them, or break file uploads. This tool lets you look up the correct MIME type for any file extension, or find which extensions correspond to a given content type. It includes hundreds of MIME types covering images, audio, video, documents, fonts, and application-specific formats.

faqs.q: What is a MIME type?
faqs.a: A MIME type is a string like 'text/html' or 'image/png' that tells the browser or client how to interpret and display a file. It consists of a type and subtype separated by a slash.

faqs.q: How do I find the MIME type for a file extension?
faqs.a: Type the file extension (e.g., .pdf, .webp) into the search box. The tool will show the corresponding MIME type and category.

faqs.q: What MIME type should I use for JSON?
faqs.a: Use 'application/json' for JSON data. For JSON with a specific schema, you can use vendor types like 'application/vnd.api+json'.

howToUseSteps: Enter a file extension (e.g., .svg) or MIME type (e.g., image/svg+xml)
Browse the results showing matching types and extensions
Click on any result to see full details
Copy the MIME type string for use in your code
useCases: Setting correct Content-Type headers in web servers
Configuring file upload validation rules
Debugging browser file rendering issues
Building file type detection in applications

escape-unescape.seoContent: Character escaping converts special characters into safe representations to prevent injection attacks and parsing errors. HTML escaping converts characters like < > & into entities (< > &). JavaScript escaping handles quotes and backslashes in strings. JSON escaping ensures strings are valid within JSON documents. This tool supports all three escaping modes and their reverse operations. It is essential for security-conscious developers who need to sanitize user input, build safe HTML output, or debug encoded strings in logs and API responses.

faqs.q: What is the difference between HTML and JavaScript escaping?
faqs.a: HTML escaping converts < > & " to HTML entities for safe display in web pages. JavaScript escaping adds backslashes before quotes, newlines, and special characters for safe use in JS strings.

faqs.q: Why do I need to escape strings?
faqs.a: Unescaped strings can cause XSS (cross-site scripting) attacks in HTML, syntax errors in JavaScript, or invalid JSON. Escaping ensures special characters are treated as data, not code.

faqs.q: Can I unescape encoded strings back to plain text?
faqs.a: Yes. Switch to Unescape mode and paste the encoded string. The tool will convert escape sequences back to their original characters.

howToUseSteps: Select the escaping format: HTML, JavaScript, or JSON
Choose Escape or Unescape mode
Paste your text into the input area

ip-calculator.seoContent: IP subnetting divides a network into smaller subnetworks to improve performance and security. Understanding subnets is critical for network administrators, DevOps engineers, and anyone configuring cloud infrastructure. This calculator takes an IP address with a CIDR prefix (e.g., 192.168.1.0/24) and instantly computes the subnet mask, network address, broadcast address, first and last usable host, and total number of hosts. It supports both IPv4 addresses and various CIDR notations from /8 to /30. All calculations are done locally in your browser.

faqs.q: What is CIDR notation?
faqs.a: CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing) notation like /24 indicates how many bits are used for the network portion of an IP address. /24 means 24 network bits and 8 host bits, allowing 254 usable hosts.

faqs.q: How do I calculate the number of hosts in a subnet?
faqs.a: The formula is 2^(32-prefix) - 2 for IPv4. The subtraction accounts for the network address and broadcast address. A /24 subnet has 2^8 - 2 = 254 usable hosts.

faqs.q: What is the difference between network and broadcast address?
faqs.a: The network address is the first address in a subnet (all host bits 0) and identifies the subnet. The broadcast address is the last (all host bits 1) and sends packets to all hosts in the subnet.

howToUseSteps: Enter an IP address (e.g., 192.168.1.100)
Enter the CIDR prefix length (e.g., /24) or subnet mask
View the calculated network address, broadcast, and host range
Copy any value you need for your network configuration

fake-data.seoContent: Generating realistic test data is essential for software development, QA testing, and database seeding. Using real personal data for testing creates privacy risks and compliance issues with regulations like GDPR. This tool generates fake but realistic names, email addresses, phone numbers, physical addresses, and other data types. All data is generated randomly in your browser using established patterns — no real personal information is used. You can generate single records or bulk data sets, and copy the results in various formats for use in your applications.

hmac-generator.name: ตัวสร้าง HMAC
hmac-generator.pageTitle: ตัวสร้าง HMAC
hmac-generator.pageDescription: สร้างลายเซ็น HMAC ด้วย SHA-256 หรือ SHA-1 ฟรี ไม่ต้องสมัครสมาชิก
hmac-generator.seoContent: HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code) combines a cryptographic hash function with a secret key to verify both data integrity and authenticity. Unlike simple hashing, HMAC requires the secret key to generate and verify signatures, making it resistant to tampering. HMAC-SHA256 is the most commonly used variant and is required by many APIs and webhook systems (Stripe, GitHub, Shopify). This tool generates HMAC signatures using SHA-1, SHA-256, or SHA-512 algorithms. Enter your message and secret key, and get the signature in hexadecimal or Base64 format. All computation happens locally.

faqs.q: What is the difference between HMAC and a regular hash?
faqs.a: A regular hash (like SHA-256) only takes a message as input. HMAC also requires a secret key, so only parties who know the key can generate or verify the signature. This prevents tampering.

faqs.q: Which HMAC algorithm should I use?
faqs.a: HMAC-SHA256 is the most common and recommended choice. It offers strong security and is required by most modern APIs. Use SHA-1 only for legacy compatibility.

faqs.q: How do I verify a webhook signature with HMAC?
faqs.a: Compute the HMAC of the webhook payload using your secret key, then compare it to the signature in the webhook header. If they match, the webhook is authentic and untampered.

howToUseSteps: Enter or paste the message to sign
Enter the secret key
Select the hash algorithm (SHA-256, SHA-1, or SHA-512)
Copy the generated HMAC signature in hex or Base64
useCases: Verifying webhook signatures from payment providers
Signing API requests for authentication
Generating message authentication codes for secure communication
Testing HMAC implementations during development

url-parser.seoContent: URLs (Uniform Resource Locators) contain multiple components: protocol (https), hostname, port, pathname, query parameters, and fragment hash. Understanding URL structure is essential for web development, API design, and debugging network requests. This tool breaks any URL into its individual components for easy inspection. It decodes percent-encoded characters, parses query strings into key-value pairs, and validates URL format. Useful for debugging redirect chains, analyzing tracking parameters, and understanding complex API endpoints.

faqs.q: What are the parts of a URL?
faqs.a: A URL consists of: protocol (https://), hostname (example.com), port (:8080), pathname (/api/users), query string (?id=123&sort=name), and fragment hash (#section).

faqs.q: How are query parameters parsed?
faqs.a: Query parameters start after the ? character and are separated by &. Each parameter is a key=value pair. Values may be percent-encoded for special characters.

faqs.q: Does it handle encoded URLs?
faqs.a: Yes. The tool automatically decodes percent-encoded characters (like %20 for spaces) and displays the decoded values alongside the raw encoded form.

howToUseSteps: Paste a complete URL into the input field
View the parsed components: protocol, host, path, query, hash
Inspect individual query parameters in the table
Copy any component value you need
useCases: Debugging complex API endpoint URLs
Analyzing UTM tracking parameters in marketing URLs
Extracting query parameters from redirect URLs
Validating URL format before using in applications

binary-text.name: ตัวแปลงข้อความ ↔ ไบนารี
binary-text.description: แปลงข้อความเป็นไบนารีและกลับกัน
binary-text.pageTitle: ตัวแปลงข้อความเป็นไบนารี
binary-text.pageDescription: แปลงข้อความเป็นไบนารีและไบนารีเป็นข้อความ ฟรี ไม่ต้องสมัครสมาชิก
binary-text.seoContent: Binary representation is the foundation of all digital computing. Every character you see on screen is stored as a sequence of 0s and 1s. This tool converts text to its binary representation and back. Each character is converted to its UTF-8 binary encoding, displayed as 8-bit groups. It supports all Unicode characters including emoji and characters from non-Latin scripts. The tool is useful for learning about character encoding, debugging encoding issues, and understanding how computers store text data at the lowest level.

faqs.q: How does text to binary conversion work?
faqs.a: Each character is converted to its Unicode code point, then encoded as binary digits. ASCII characters use 8 bits (1 byte), while other Unicode characters may use 16 or 32 bits.

faqs.q: What encoding does this tool use?
faqs.a: The tool uses UTF-8 encoding by default, which is backward-compatible with ASCII and supports all Unicode characters.

faqs.q: Can I convert binary back to text?
faqs.a: Yes. Switch to Binary → Text mode and paste your binary string (space-separated 8-bit groups). The tool will decode it back to readable text.

howToUseSteps: Select the conversion direction: Text → Binary or Binary → Text
Enter your text or binary string in the input area
View the converted output instantly
Copy the result to your clipboard
useCases: Learning about character encoding and binary representation
Debugging encoding issues in text processing
Creating binary art or encoded messages
Understanding how computers store and process text

pem-decoder.description: ถอดรหัสใบรับรอง PEM
pem-decoder.pageTitle: ตัวถอดรหัสใบรับรอง PEM
pem-decoder.pageDescription: ถอดรหัสใบรับรองในรูปแบบ PEM ฟรี ไม่ต้องสมัครสมาชิก
pem-decoder.seoContent: PEM (Privacy Enhanced Mail) is the most common format for SSL/TLS certificates, private keys, and certificate chains. PEM files are Base64-encoded with header and footer lines like -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----. This tool decodes PEM-formatted certificates and displays all X.509 fields: subject, issuer, validity dates, serial number, signature algorithm, public key details, and extensions like Subject Alternative Names (SANs). It is essential for DevOps engineers managing SSL certificates, debugging TLS handshake failures, and verifying certificate chains.

faqs.q: What information can I see from a PEM certificate?
faqs.a: You can see the subject (domain name), issuer (CA), validity dates, serial number, signature algorithm, public key type and size, and extensions like SANs and key usage.

faqs.q: Is it safe to paste my certificate here?
faqs.a: Yes. All decoding happens locally in your browser. Your certificate data is never sent to any server. Note: never paste private keys in any online tool.

faqs.q: What is the difference between PEM and DER format?
faqs.a: PEM is Base64-encoded text with header/footer lines, readable in any text editor. DER is the raw binary format. This tool only handles PEM format.

howToUseSteps: Paste your PEM-formatted certificate (including BEGIN/END lines)
View the decoded certificate details instantly
Check the validity dates, subject, and issuer information
Verify Subject Alternative Names (SANs) for your domains
useCases: Verifying SSL certificate details before installation
Checking certificate expiration dates
Debugging TLS handshake and certificate chain issues
Inspecting certificate SANs for multi-domain coverage

bcrypt-generator.name: ตัวสร้างแฮช Bcrypt
bcrypt-generator.description: สร้างแฮชรหัสผ่าน bcrypt ที่กำหนดค่าได้
bcrypt-generator.pageTitle: ตัวสร้างแฮช Bcrypt
bcrypt-generator.pageDescription: สร้างแฮชรหัสผ่าน bcrypt ด้วยปัจจัยต้นทุนที่กำหนดค่าได้ ฟรี ไม่ต้องสมัครสมาชิก
bcrypt-generator.seoContent: Bcrypt is a password hashing function designed to be slow and computationally expensive, making brute-force attacks impractical. Unlike fast hashes like MD5 or SHA-256, bcrypt incorporates a configurable cost factor that controls how many iterations are performed. Each increase in cost doubles the computation time. Bcrypt also automatically generates and embeds a random salt, preventing rainbow table attacks. This tool generates bcrypt hashes from passwords with your chosen cost factor (typically 10-12 for web applications). It can also verify if a password matches a given bcrypt hash. All processing happens locally.

faqs.q: What cost factor should I use for bcrypt?
faqs.a: A cost of 10-12 is recommended for most web applications, balancing security and performance. Cost 10 takes about 100ms per hash. Each increment doubles the time.

faqs.q: Is bcrypt better than SHA-256 for passwords?
faqs.a: Yes. SHA-256 is designed to be fast, which makes it vulnerable to brute-force attacks. Bcrypt is intentionally slow and includes a built-in salt, making it much more secure for password storage.

faqs.q: Can I verify a password against a bcrypt hash?
faqs.a: Yes. Enter the password and the bcrypt hash, and the tool will tell you if they match. The salt is embedded in the hash, so no separate salt is needed.

howToUseSteps: Enter the password you want to hash
Set the cost factor (default: 10)
Click Generate to create the bcrypt hash
Copy the hash for use in your application's database
useCases: Generating password hashes for user registration systems
Verifying stored passwords during authentication
Testing bcrypt implementations in your application
Comparing different cost factors for performance tuning

json-to-graphql.name: JSON to GraphQL
json-to-graphql.description: Convert JSON data to GraphQL schema definitions
json-to-graphql.pageDescription: Convert JSON to GraphQL type definitions online. Generate accurate GraphQL schemas from JSON data with nested types and arrays. Free and instant.
json-to-graphql.seoContent: GraphQL uses a strongly-typed schema to define the shape of data available through an API. When designing a GraphQL API, you often start with sample JSON data from an existing REST endpoint or database. This tool analyzes your JSON structure and generates the corresponding GraphQL type definitions. It maps JavaScript types to GraphQL scalars (String, Int, Float, Boolean), creates separate type blocks for nested objects, and handles arrays as list types. The generated schema can serve as a starting point for your GraphQL server implementation. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.q: How does JSON to GraphQL conversion work?
faqs.a: The tool analyzes your JSON structure and maps each field to the appropriate GraphQL type. Strings become String, numbers become Int or Float, booleans become Boolean, nested objects become separate types, and arrays become list types.

faqs.q: Does it generate a complete GraphQL schema?
faqs.a: It generates type definitions that you can use in your schema. You may need to add custom resolvers, mutations, and input types depending on your API design.

faqs.q: How are nested objects handled?
faqs.a: Nested objects are extracted into separate named types. For example, a user with an address object will generate both a User type and an Address type.

faqs.q: Is the output ready to use in a GraphQL server?
faqs.a: The generated types are valid GraphQL SDL (Schema Definition Language) and can be used directly in servers like Apollo, Yoga, or any SDL-first GraphQL framework.

howToUseSteps: Paste your JSON data into the input panel
Set the root type name (default: Root)
Click Convert to generate GraphQL types
Copy the schema into your GraphQL server
useCases: Designing GraphQL schemas from existing REST API responses
Prototyping GraphQL types from sample data
Migrating REST APIs to GraphQL
Generating type definitions for GraphQL code generators

json-to-java.name: JSON to Java Class
json-to-java.description: Convert JSON data to Java class definitions
json-to-java.pageDescription: Convert JSON to Java POJO classes online. Generate Java classes with getters, setters, and Lombok support. Free, fast, and private.
json-to-java.seoContent: Java's strong type system requires defining classes before deserializing JSON data. Manually writing Java POJOs (Plain Old Java Objects) for complex JSON APIs is tedious and error-prone. This tool analyzes your JSON and generates complete Java class definitions with proper field types, constructors, getters, and setters. It supports Lombok's @Data annotation to reduce boilerplate. Nested objects become separate classes, arrays become List<Type>, and null values are handled with nullable types. All processing happens in your browser.

faqs.q: How do I convert JSON to Java classes?
faqs.a: Paste your JSON data, set a root class name, and click Convert. The tool generates Java POJO classes with proper types, fields, constructors, getters, and setters.

faqs.q: What is the Lombok option?
faqs.a: When enabled, the tool adds Lombok's @Data annotation which auto-generates getters, setters, toString, equals, and hashCode methods, significantly reducing boilerplate code.

faqs.q: How are arrays handled?
faqs.a: JSON arrays are converted to List<Type> with appropriate generic types. The tool adds the java.util.List import automatically.

faqs.q: Can I use the generated classes directly?
faqs.a: Yes. The output is valid Java code ready to use with Jackson, Gson, or any JSON library. Just copy into .java files.

howToUseSteps: Paste your JSON data into the input panel
Set the root class name (default: Root)
Toggle Lombok support if desired
Copy the generated Java classes into your project

Generating model classes for Spring Boot applications

json-to-kotlin.pageTitle: JSON to Kotlin Data Class Converter
json-to-kotlin.pageDescription: Convert JSON to Kotlin data classes online. Generate idiomatic Kotlin code with nullable types and proper type inference. Free and instant.
json-to-kotlin.seoContent: Kotlin data classes provide a concise way to define typed data models. When working with JSON APIs in Kotlin (especially on Android), you need data classes that match the JSON structure. This tool analyzes your JSON and generates idiomatic Kotlin data classes with proper type inference. It handles nullable types for null values, uses List<Type> for arrays, and creates separate data classes for nested objects. The generated code works seamlessly with Kotlinx.serialization, Moshi, or Gson. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.q: How do I convert JSON to Kotlin data classes?
faqs.a: Paste your JSON, set the root class name, and click Convert. The tool generates Kotlin data classes with proper types for each field.

faqs.q: How are nullable types handled?
faqs.a: Fields with null values are typed as nullable (String?). You can also enable the nullable option to make all fields nullable.

faqs.q: Does it work with Android development?
faqs.a: Yes. The generated data classes are compatible with Retrofit, Moshi, Gson, and Kotlinx.serialization commonly used in Android apps.

faqs.q: How are nested objects converted?
faqs.a: Nested JSON objects become separate Kotlin data classes. For example, an address field generates both a Root data class and an Address data class.

json-to-csharp.description: Convert JSON data to C# class definitions
json-to-csharp.pageDescription: Convert JSON to C# classes online. Generate C# class definitions with proper types and optional namespace. Free, fast, and private.
json-to-csharp.seoContent: C#'s strong type system is central to .NET development. This tool analyzes your JSON data and generates C# class definitions with correct property types (string, int, double, bool, List<T>), PascalCase naming, and optional namespace wrapping. Nested objects become separate classes, and nullable types are used for null values. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.q: How do I convert JSON to C# classes?
faqs.a: Paste your JSON data, set a root class name, optionally add a namespace, and click Convert. The tool generates C# classes with proper property types.

faqs.q: Does it work with System.Text.Json?
faqs.a: Yes. The generated classes use standard C# properties that work with both System.Text.Json and Newtonsoft.Json (Json.NET).

faqs.q: How are arrays handled?
faqs.a: JSON arrays are converted to List<Type>. The tool adds using System.Collections.Generic when List types are present.

faqs.q: Can I add a namespace?
faqs.a: Yes. Enter a namespace name and the generated classes will be wrapped in a namespace block with proper indentation.

faqs.a: Fields with null values are typed as Option<String>. This allows the field to be None when the value is null in JSON.

cron-expression-generator.faq3q: How do I run a job every 5 minutes?
cron-expression-generator.faq3a: Use the expression */5 * * * *. The */5 in the minute field means every 5 minutes, and * in other fields means any hour, day, month, and weekday.
cron-expression-generator.faq4a: Yes. Use commas to separate values (e.g., 0 9,17 * * * runs at 9 AM and 5 PM daily). Use hyphens for ranges (e.g., 1-5 for Monday through Friday).

faqs.q: How is TOML different from YAML?
faqs.a: TOML uses explicit syntax with brackets and equals signs, making it less ambiguous than YAML. TOML doesn't rely on indentation and has clearer rules for data types, making it harder to make mistakes.

about.title: เกี่ยวกับ DevToolBox
about.intro: DevToolBox คือชุดเครื่องมือนักพัฒนาออนไลน์ฟรี สร้างมาสำหรับโปรแกรมเมอร์ นักออกแบบ และทุกคนที่ทำงานกับข้อมูล
about.missionTitle: พันธกิจของเรา
about.missionText: เราเชื่อว่าเครื่องมือสำหรับนักพัฒนาควรฟรี เร็ว และเป็นส่วนตัว เครื่องมือทุกตัวบน DevToolBox ประมวลผลข้อมูลทั้งหมดในเบราว์เซอร์ของคุณ — ไม่มีข้อมูลใดถูกส่งไปยังเซิร์ฟเวอร์เลย
about.feature1: เครื่องมือนักพัฒนาสำคัญกว่า 100 รายการ
about.feature2: ประมวลผลฝั่งไคลเอนต์ 100% — ข้อมูลของคุณไม่ออกจากเบราว์เซอร์
about.feature3: ไม่ต้องสมัครสมาชิก ไม่มีบัญชีผู้ใช้ ไม่มีการติดตาม
about.feature4: ใช้ได้บนเดสก์ท็อป แท็บเล็ต และมือถือ
about.feature5: เร็วและเบา

privacy.title: นโยบายความเป็นส่วนตัว
privacy.intro: ที่ DevToolBox ความเป็นส่วนตัวของคุณคือสิ่งสำคัญที่สุดของเรา
privacy.dataTitle: การประมวลผลข้อมูล
privacy.dataText: เครื่องมือทั้งหมดบน DevToolBox ประมวลผลข้อมูลทั้งหมดในเบราว์เซอร์ของคุณ เราไม่เคยส่งข้อมูลของคุณไปยังเซิร์ฟเวอร์ใดๆ ข้อมูลที่คุณป้อนไม่ออกจากอุปกรณ์ของคุณ
privacy.cookiesText: เราอาจใช้คุกกี้เพื่อวัตถุประสงค์ด้านการวิเคราะห์ (เช่น Google Analytics) และการโฆษณา (เช่น Google AdSense) เพื่อทำความเข้าใจวิธีที่ผู้เข้าชมใช้เว็บไซต์ของเราและเพื่อแสดงโฆษณาที่เกี่ยวข้อง บริการของบุคคลที่สามเหล่านี้อาจเก็บข้อมูลการใช้งานแบบไม่ระบุตัวตน
privacy.adsText: เราแสดงโฆษณาผ่าน Google AdSense เพื่อสนับสนุนการดำเนินงานฟรีของเว็บไซต์นี้ AdSense อาจใช้คุกกี้และ web beacon เพื่อแสดงโฆษณาตามการเข้าชมก่อนหน้าของคุณ
privacy.thirdPartyTitle: บริการของบุคคลที่สาม
privacy.thirdPartyText: เราใช้บริการของบุคคลที่สามดังต่อไปนี้:
privacy.thirdParty1: Google Analytics — สำหรับสถิติการใช้งานแบบไม่ระบุตัวตน
privacy.thirdParty2: Google AdSense — สำหรับแสดงโฆษณา
privacy.changesTitle: การเปลี่ยนแปลง
privacy.changesText: เราอาจอัปเดตนโยบายความเป็นส่วนตัวนี้เป็นครั้งคราว กลับมาตรวจสอบเป็นระยะเพื่อดูการอัปเดต
privacy.contactText: มีคำถามเกี่ยวกับนโยบายนี้? เปิด issue ได้ที่ GitHub repository ของเรา
